jobs.title: Associate Director, IOCC Transformation & Innovation
jobs.description:
Toronto Pearson is transforming. Now’s the time for your career to fly.

The Greater Toronto Airports Authority (GTAA) is a unique and dynamic place to work, with a bold plan to make Toronto Pearson, Canada’s leading global hub airport, a global leader in airport performance, customer care and sustainability. Together with our partners, approximately 2,100 GTAA employees are working to create a next-generation airport by innovating in all we do and striving for the most uplifting, safe and efficient experience for our passengers – all while championing the prosperity of our people, the community we call home, and our aviation partners. Join us on our journey together, as we put the joy back into travel and make Toronto Pearson the chosen place to fly and work.

What's in it for you?

An opportunity to grow, develop, and thrive within a dynamic, and fast-growing company alongside thoughtful and passionate individuals dedicated to their work and community.
Comprehensive benefits, including a flexible retirement program with employer matching, along with voluntary savings options (RRSP, TFSA, and Non-Registered Savings Plans).
A flexible work environment, continuous internal and external learning opportunities, and a meaningful reward and recognition program.

What can you expect from this position?

Reporting to the Director, IOCC, the Associate Director, IOCC Transformation & Innovation is responsible for leading the transformation of Toronto Pearson's Integrated Operations Control Centre into a predictive, technology-enabled, collaborative airport operations model. This role will translate operational modernization strategy into sustainable capabilities across people, processes, technology, data, governance, and partner collaboration.

As a strategic leader, you will drive the development and implementation of innovative operating models, digital capabilities, analytics, performance frameworks, and transformation initiatives that improve operational resilience, passenger experience, airport performance, and decision-making. You will lead a multidisciplinary team and work across the airport ecosystem to deliver operational excellence and future-ready capabilities that support one of Canada's most complex transportation environments.

As an Associate Director, IOCC Transformation and Innovation, you will:

Lead the development and execution of a multi-year transformation roadmap that advances airport operational excellence.
Drive transformation initiatives from concept through implementation, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
Establish innovative operating models, governance structures, and collaborative decision-making practices across airport stakeholders.
Lead the evolution of operational systems, digital tools, analytics platforms, and data-driven decision-support capabilities.
Develop and govern airport-wide performance frameworks, key performance indicators, and service level agreements.
Champion innovation through the evaluation and adoption of emerging technologies, industry best practices, and new operating models.
Provide strategic operational planning, forecasting, and analytics capabilities that support proactive and predictive operations.
Partner with internal and external stakeholders to align priorities, improve performance, and deliver transformation initiatives.
Lead and develop teams responsible for transformation, operational planning, systems, digital enablement, and business analytics.
Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.

This is the role for you, if you have:

8+ years of progressive leadership experience, including experience leading large-scale transformation, modernization, or technology-enabled change programs.
5+ years of people leadership experience within a complex matrix environment.
Experience within aviation, transportation, logistics, infrastructure, operations, or similarly complex operational environments.
Demonstrated success leading cross-functional programs involving business, technology, operational, regulatory, and external stakeholders.
Experience delivering operational systems, analytics capabilities, digital tools, and business transformation initiatives.
Strong change management, stakeholder engagement, strategic planning, and business transformation capabilities.
Strong understanding of data, analytics, performance measurement, and continuous improvement.
Bachelor’s degree in aviation management, Engineering, Business Administration, Operations Management, Information Systems, or a related discipline.
Professional certifications such as PMP, Lean Six Sigma, Prosci, Agile, or Data Analytics.
Valid Ontario Driver's License.
Ability to obtain and retain Transportation Security Clearance at the designated level for the position.

The GTAA is committed to Employment Equity and maintaining a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive.

This position is exempt from Ontario's 2026 pay transparency requirements under Regulation 476/24.

jobs.description:
Career opportunities are presented in the language received.

Nunavut Housing Corporation | Iqaluit, Nunavut | Full-time

About Nunavut Housing Corporation

The Nunavut Housing Corporation (NHC) is an arm’s-length public agency of the Government of Nunavut (GN) and the driving force in housing policy, program delivery, and construction across Nunavut’s 25 communities. With an operating budget of more than $230 million and a capital budget of approximately $171 million, NHC is leading Nunavut 3000, an estimated $1.6 billion plan to build 3,000 new homes over 10 years.

About The Role

Reporting to the President & CEO and serving on the Corporate Executive Committee, the VP, Finance and Corporate Services leads finance, human resources, IT, and policy and strategic planning, with five direct reports and functional oversight for approximately 350 employees across 25 Local Housing Organizations (LHOs). The VP also serves as President & CEO as required.

Key Responsibilities

Financial leadership: Steward NHC’s financial health, advise the executive team, and represent NHC with the GN, CMHC, Cabinet, the Financial Management Board, and the Legislature.
People and culture: Lead a newly established HR function and build a strong workforce, with a deliberate focus on Inuit employment, training, and development.
Technology: Oversee the systems and IT services that support NHC and all 25 LHOs, strengthening digital capacity and data security for growth.
Policy and strategy: Shape NHC’s policies, plans, and research, and support the Minister’s office.

What We’re Looking For

A dynamic, transformational leader who will modernize and integrate corporate services, simplifying processes and raising performance as NHC grows.
Hands-on and ready to act, making an immediate impact by strengthening the finance function and building depth across the team.
An innovative, steady executive who brings fresh approaches to partnerships, funding, and procurement, and leads with confidence through change.
A coach and people builder who develops talent, especially Nunavut Inuit, and communicates complex issues clearly and respectfully.

Qualifications

CPA designation and at least 10 years of progressive senior finance and management experience, ideally in the public sector, a Crown corporation, or housing.
Strong command of public-sector budgeting, financial administration, and audit.
Knowledge of Nunavut, the Nunavut Agreement, and the roles of Inuit organizations.
Housing experience and fluency in more than one of Nunavut’s official languages are assets; an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Priority will be given to Nunavut Inuit who self-identify as being enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement, in accordance with the GN Priority Hiring Policy.

Salary: $160,374 to $229,106 per year, plus Northern Allowance and subsidized housing.

Closing date: November 25, 2026.

This position is a Position of Trust, a criminal record check required. AI will not be used in candidate screening.

To apply, submit your application to Phelps by clicking: https://phelpsgroup.ca/careers/31837/nunavut-housing-corporation-vp-finance-corp-services/apply/(opens in a new tab)

jobs.title: Director, Fraud Analytics & Risk Management
jobs.description:
At Manulife Bank, protecting our customers, advisors, and business from financial crime is a critical strategic priority. As Director, Fraud Analytics & Risk Management, you will lead the Bank's fraud analytics and intelligence capabilities, leveraging advanced data analytics, customer risk modeling, and fraud technologies to proactively identify, detect, and mitigate fraud across all banking products, channels, and customer journeys.

This role is responsible for developing a data-driven fraud management ecosystem that delivers strong customer protection while enabling frictionless banking experiences. Working closely with Operations, Risk, Technology, Digital, Data & Analytics, and external partners, you will drive innovative solutions that enhance fraud detection, strengthen customer risk management, and improve fraud prevention outcomes.

Reporting to the AVP/VP, Fraud Strategy & Operations, you will play a key leadership role in shaping the future state fraud capability at Manulife Bank.

Position Responsibilities

Lead Fraud Analytics & Intelligence

Develop and execute the Bank's fraud analytics strategy across deposits, lending, mortgages, payments, digital banking, contact centre, and advisor channels.
Establish proactive monitoring and analytical capabilities to detect emerging fraud risks, customer scams, account takeover attacks, identity theft, synthetic identities, mule activity, and organized fraud networks.
Leverage internal and external data sources to identify fraud trends, vulnerabilities, and opportunities for control enhancement.
Lead fraud intelligence and root-cause analysis activities to continuously improve detection and prevention effectiveness.
Build meaningful analytics, dashboards, and executive reporting to support fraud management decision-making.

Own Customer Risk Scoring & Fraud Decisioning

Design, develop, and continuously optimize customer fraud risk scoring models across the customer lifecycle.
Enhance risk-based authentication, transaction monitoring, and fraud intervention strategies.
Leverage behavioural analytics, device intelligence, digital signals, transaction patterns, and external intelligence to improve customer risk segmentation.
Monitor model performance and ensure appropriate governance, oversight, validation, and recalibration.
Support development of real-time fraud detection and decisioning capabilities as the Bank evolves its payments and digital banking ecosystem.

Advance Fraud Technology Capabilities

Lead evaluation, implementation, and optimization of fraud technology solutions that strengthen the Bank's fraud prevention capabilities.
Partner with vendors to implement prevention and detection fraud toolkits
Develop business cases and strategic recommendations for fraud technology investments.
Manage vendor relationships, performance expectations, and ongoing solution effectiveness reviews.

Strengthen Fraud Risk Management

Lead comprehensive fraud risk assessments across products, processes, channels, and strategic initiatives.
Partner with Enterprise Risk Management and Compliance teams to ensure fraud risks are appropriately identified, measured, monitored, and mitigated.
Define and maintain fraud risk indicators, thresholds, risk appetite metrics, and reporting frameworks.
Identify control gaps and drive remediation strategies.
Support regulatory, audit, and governance reviews related to fraud risk management.

Enable Data-Driven Fraud Prevention

Partner with Analytics on developing predictive models to improve fraud detection and prevention outcomes.
Leverage machine learning, network analytics, behavioural analytics, anomaly detection, and AI-enabled capabilities where appropriate.
Balance fraud loss reduction objectives with customer experience considerations.
Translate complex analytical findings into actionable business recommendations for senior leadership.

Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team

Build and lead a team of fraud analytics, fraud intelligence, and risk professionals.
Foster a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, accountability, and customer focus.
Coach and develop talent while building future fraud analytics capabilities for the Bank.
Serve as a trusted advisor to executives and stakeholders on fraud risk trends, emerging threats, and mitigation strategies.

Required Qualifications

University degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Business, Finance, Risk Management, or a related discipline.
10+ years of experience in fraud analytics, fraud risk management, financial crimes, banking analytics, or advanced data analytics.
Deep understanding of fraud risks across retail banking products and customer journeys.
Experience developing fraud detection models, customer risk scoring frameworks, and fraud monitoring programs.
Experience managing fraud technology vendors and implementing fraud

Preferred Qualifications

Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills.
Graduate degree in a quantitative or business discipline. Professional certifications such as:
Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE)
Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS)
Certified Analytics Professional (CAP)
Experience with machine learning and AI-enabled fraud detection solutions.
Experience supporting real-time payments, digital banking, and emerging payment ecosystems.
Experience working with SQL, Python, SAS, Power BI, Tableau, machine learning and predictive analytics tools, fraud detection and case management platforms, identity verification technologies, behavioural analytics solutions, and device intelligence platforms to support data-driven decision-making, fraud prevention, and operational effectiveness.

Success in This Role

You Will Be Successful If You

Demonstrate strategic thinking and strong business acumen.
Drive measurable improvements in fraud control effectiveness.
Proactively identify emerging fraud risks before they impact customers.
Build strong partnerships across the Bank and Enterprise.
Translate complex fraud risks into actionable business recommendations.
Balance customer experience, operational efficiency, regulatory requirements, and risk management objectives

When You Join Our Team

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.
We’ll recognize and support you in a flexible environment where well-being and inclusion are more than just words.
As part of our global team, we’ll support you in shaping the future you want to see.

The role being advertised is an existing vacancy.

jobs.title: Finance Director
jobs.description:
About Toronto Metropolitan

For more than 75 years, Toronto Metropolitan University (formerly known as Ryerson University) has been shaping the next generation of leaders through its uniquely innovative, entrepreneurial and career-focused approach to higher education. Driven by bold leadership, cutting-edge research and a deep commitment to academic excellence, TMU collaborates with students, faculties, staff and partners to push boundaries, reimagine solutions and create meaningful change in an increasingly interconnected world.

For a more in-depth understanding of our vision, core values and ongoing work, please see our academic plan

TMU welcomes those who have demonstrated a commitment to upholding the values of equity, diversity, and inclusion and will assist us in realizing the benefits of embedding these values into the work at every level and in every unit of the university. In addition, to correct the conditions of disadvantage in employment in Canada and to bring lived experiences to the work, we encourage applications from members of equity deserving groups that have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including First Nations, Métis and Inuit Peoples in Canada, First Nations Peoples in the United States, racialized people, Black people, persons with disabilities, women, and 2SLGBTQ+ people. Preference will be given to candidates with lived experiences as people from equity deserving groups, as well as experience working with these communities with which the University works every day. Please note that all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply and we welcome newcomers and immigrants to Canada.

In April 2022, the university announced its new name of Toronto Metropolitan University. Learn more about our next chapter.

About The School Of Medicine

It’s time to transform medical education. Toronto Metropolitan University’s School of Medicine has been designed from the ground up to shift the paradigm of healthcare delivery and improve the well-being of individuals, families and communities. With a community-driven, intentionally inclusive approach, the new school is training doctors whose cultural awareness and humility are as crucial as their medical skills.

Led by Dr. Teresa M. Chan, a forward-thinking educational leader, TMU’s School of Medicine draws on the university’s commitment to community, equity, and innovation to address rapidly changing healthcare needs. The school will train a new generation of physicians who are ready to learn, to adapt, and ultimately to be agents of change.

The Opportunity

We are hiring a Finance Director to join the School of Medicine! This newly created role leads the development and implementation of school-wide financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and resource management strategies that advance the academic, research, and operational priorities of the School of Medicine.

Serving as a trusted strategic advisor, the position provides expert financial counsel to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Dean, and senior leadership by assessing long-term financial implications, recommending evidence-based solutions, and ensuring alignment with broader University policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.

This role oversees the financial operations of the School of Medicine, supporting budgeting, reporting, financial compliance, and informed decision-making. he Director also provides financial and advisory support to the Integrated Health Centre, including support for external financial reporting and audit requirements,, in close collaboration with TMU Financial Services and the University Planning Office.

In addition, the Director conducts financial research and analysis to inform policy development and long-term planning, and represents the CAO and the School of Medicine in TMU-wide planning discussions and committees.

Responsibilities Include

Financial planning, budgeting and management

Provides financial advice, analysis, and decision-support to departments within the School of Medicine to support budget development, financial planning, forecasting, and effective resource management.
Manages day-to-day financial activities for the School of Medicine, including monitoring and reconciling operating and payroll expenditures, and ensures that actual financial results reconcile with approved targets
Collaborates with the University Planning Office (UPO) to support the annual budget development process for the SoM.

Payroll Administration and Financial Oversight (SoM Residents and IHC Employees)

Oversees, reviews, and approves biweekly payroll registers before the third-party vendor releases payments and monthly reconciliations. Investigate unusual variances, adjustments, and exceptions.
Monitors payroll funding requirements, forecast upcoming payroll obligations, and ensure sufficient funds are available in the designated bank account before each payroll withdrawal
Oversee the processes, systems, and internal controls supporting the administration of payroll, benefits, and expense claims for medical learners (residents) and Integrated Health Centre (IHC) staff.
Provide leadership and oversight to staff responsible for processing payroll, benefits, and expenses, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with applicable policies and requirements.
Establish and maintain effective procedures, workflows, and controls to support reliable and efficient administration of these functions.

Strategy and external collaboration

Conducts financial research and analysis to support the Dean and CAO in the development of a funding model for the School of Medicine and the Integrated Health Centres (IHC).
Monitors SOM activities relevant to external funding and reporting obligations, and ensures timely information sharing with relevant stakeholders.
Develops and implements a strategic roadmap for School-wide financial forecasting, planning, and internal financial controls, including long-term budget plan for the SoM that supports the academic, research, and operational priorities.
Provides expert analysis and strategic advice on financial risk management for proposed and approved School initiatives.

Financial evaluation and program analysis

Conducts financial evaluations of revenue-generating proposals and new initiatives, and analyzes program costing reports.

Accounting management, reporting & analysis

Manages a wide range of operating, trust, and project accounts (research and non-research) for the SoM and IHC.
Supports University-wide interim and year-end financial statement audits by coordinating SoM responses, and responds to audit inquiries related to IHC and SoM special purpose audits.
Leads the planning and execution of financial analysis to support strategic and operational decisions, and oversees the development and maintenance of statistical analysis systems and integrated financial tracking tools.

HR management

Manages and supervises staff, assigns and prioritises tasks, establishes goals, sets expectations and evaluates performance.

Qualifications

To help us learn more about you, please provide a cover letter and resume describing how you meet the following required qualifications:

Completion of a university degree program in finance, accounting, business or public administration, or a relevant field.
A minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in financial management within a post-secondary, public sector, or MUSH (municipalities, universities, school boards, hospitals) environment, including experience managing complex budgets, government funding, and resource planning.
Equivalent experience or a combination of equivalent experience and education may be accepted in place of education.
Demonstrated work experience in statistical analysis to support forecasting, financial modelling, and program/project viability assessments.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) is an asset.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including variance analysis and financial interpretation.
Knowledge of statistical analysis measurement theory to support forecasting, modelling, and program/project viability assessments.
In-depth knowledge of accounting and finance principles and associated technical and security considerations.
Knowledge of Microsoft Excel/Google Sheet and financial systems/software applications to support modelling and reporting.
Knowledge of post-secondary education systems, funding structures and sector-specific financial issues.
Demonstrated skill in developing and implementing financial policies, procedures and processes for new or evolving business initiatives.
Strong project and time management skills in a fast-paced environment.
Effective communication skills to convey complex financial information with stakeholders.
Troubleshooting skills, particularly in identifying causes of financial variances.
Ability to work on team-based projects, and prepare and present accurate reports to senior management.
Ability to organize and manage a complex financial process with accuracy and consistency.
Systems-wide thinking skills, with ability to assess financial and operational implications across units and stakeholder groups.

Leadership Competencies

Leaders at TMU are required to demonstrate the following Leadership Competencies:

Acts with Integrity: Demonstrates behaviors aligned with high ethical standards and personal integrity and acts in accordance with TMU values.
Builds Relationships of Trust & Collaboration: Actively builds a culture of trust and fosters meaningful relationships.
Leads Inclusively: Creates an inclusive environment where everyone is respected, recognized, empowered to achieve their potential, and valued for their differences.
Demonstrates Organizational Acumen: Understands and respectfully navigates complex internal and external environments using sound judgment, diplomacy, and tact.
Drives Vision & Results: Creates and implements a vision grounded in sound decision-making to achieve desired outcomes.

As a recognized leader in the field, you act as a trusted advisor to the leadership teams and contribute to attracting, engaging, and retaining talent through competitive, equitable, and business-aligned programs.

You also ensure innovation, sound governance, regulatory compliance, and the effective management of investments related to the programs under your responsibility.

This strategic role gives you the opportunity to make a significant impact across the organization through your leadership, collaborative approach, and ability to mobilize stakeholders.

Your Role

Lead and develop a small team of specialized experts.

Act as a recognized leader and internal subject matter expert on employee benefits matters, supporting business priorities as well as talent attraction, engagement, and retention.

Define and evolve the strategies, policies, programs, and technology platforms that support the employee benefits offering.

Advise leadership teams on complex and strategic matters.

Monitor market trends to ensure a competitive and innovative benefits offering.

Collaborate with business partners to evolve programs based on the needs of the Bank and its employees.

jobs.title: Head of Finance - R&D
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Head of Finance - R&D based in Canada.

We are looking for a strategic and hands-on finance leader to oversee the financial and banking infrastructure of a portfolio of fast-growing international technology businesses.

In this role, you will shape a multi-jurisdictional banking network, strengthen payment operations, and manage complex treasury activities across multiple entities.

You will drive liquidity management, optimize foreign exchange and transaction costs, and ensure reliable cross-border financial flows.

Working closely with founders and senior leaders, you will contribute to financial strategy, business performance, and investment decisions.

You will also build scalable treasury and finance processes from the ground up while developing a high-performing operational team.

This is an opportunity to take full ownership of a complex financial ecosystem and support the growth of ambitious digital businesses in a dynamic, international environment.

Accountabilities

Responsibilities

As Head of Finance - R&D, you will lead the development and management of the financial infrastructure, treasury operations, and banking partnerships supporting international technology businesses. Your main responsibilities will include:

Banking and Payment Infrastructure
Design and implement a flexible, multi-jurisdictional banking network for international digital businesses operating under demanding compliance requirements.
Identify, negotiate with, and onboard strategic financial partners, including leading banks, Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs), Payment Service Providers (PSPs), custodians, and financial platforms.
Negotiate favorable commercial terms, including transaction fees, payment terms, foreign exchange rates, and hedging instruments.
Establish backup banking relationships and alternative payment channels to ensure uninterrupted transaction processing.

Treasury and Liquidity Management
Manage multi-currency liquidity, working capital, cash pooling, and treasury operations across a group of legal entities.
Oversee complex international transfers through SWIFT, SEPA, ACH, and other payment networks, prioritizing speed, security, and cost efficiency.
Monitor and reduce treasury expenses, including FX spreads, acquiring fees, and banking charges.

Compliance, KYC, and Regulatory Strategy
Coordinate banking due diligence and maintain effective communication with bank compliance and risk teams.
Ensure the long-term stability of banking relationships and payment flows.
Support financial restructuring, corporate changes, and related banking and compliance requirements.

Financial Systems and Executive Partnership
Build integrated treasury and financial processes from the ground up.
Partner with founders and senior leadership on unit economics, ROI analysis, and financial modeling.
Recruit, lead, and develop the treasury and operational finance team.

Requirements

The ideal candidate combines senior finance leadership experience with strong expertise in international treasury operations, banking infrastructure, and financial compliance. You should bring:

At least 5 years of experience as a CFO, VP of Finance, or Head of Treasury in fast-growing businesses.
A proven track record of opening corporate bank accounts and establishing efficient payment processes.
Deep knowledge of international AML/KYC principles, cross-border compliance, and regulatory requirements across different jurisdictions.
Practical experience managing multi-currency funds, foreign exchange exposure, financial settlement instruments, and transaction cost optimization.
Strong negotiation skills and the ability to manage complex relationships with banks, legal advisors, and financial service providers.
Advanced English proficiency (C1/C2), with the ability to lead detailed, persuasive negotiations independently.
Strong strategic thinking, financial judgment, and the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-paced, international environment.
Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with founders and executive stakeholders.

Benefits

High level of autonomy: Full ownership of the financial and banking infrastructure, with minimal unnecessary bureaucracy.
Meaningful business impact: Direct involvement in launching and scaling new technology businesses serving millions of users.
Strong professional environment: Collaboration with experienced founders and talented engineering and marketing professionals.
Dedicated platform support: Access to more than 10 specialized teams providing expertise in recruitment, communications, finance, legal matters, and other operational areas.
Founder community: Opportunities to exchange practical knowledge and experience with entrepreneurs who have successfully launched multiple businesses.
Professional communities: Access to internal groups focused on product, marketing, engineering, and payments.
Learning and development: Training programs, professional courses, and opportunities to attend industry conferences.
Healthcare: Medical insurance.
Social impact: The opportunity to contribute to initiatives supporting recovery and addressing the consequences of the war in Ukraine.

How Jobgether Works

Nunavut Housing Corporation | Iqaluit, Nunavut | Full-time

About Nunavut Housing Corporation

The Nunavut Housing Corporation (NHC) is an arm’s-length public agency of the Government of Nunavut (GN) and the driving force in housing policy, program delivery, and construction across Nunavut’s 25 communities. With an operating budget of more than $230 million and a capital budget of approximately $171 million, NHC is leading Nunavut 3000, an estimated $1.6 billion plan to build 3,000 new homes over 10 years.

About The Role

Reporting to the President & CEO and serving on the Corporate Executive Committee, the VP, Finance and Corporate Services leads finance, human resources, IT, and policy and strategic planning, with five direct reports and functional oversight for approximately 350 employees across 25 Local Housing Organizations (LHOs). The VP also serves as President & CEO as required.

Key Responsibilities

Financial leadership: Steward NHC’s financial health, advise the executive team, and represent NHC with the GN, CMHC, Cabinet, the Financial Management Board, and the Legislature.
People and culture: Lead a newly established HR function and build a strong workforce, with a deliberate focus on Inuit employment, training, and development.
Technology: Oversee the systems and IT services that support NHC and all 25 LHOs, strengthening digital capacity and data security for growth.
Policy and strategy: Shape NHC’s policies, plans, and research, and support the Minister’s office.

What We’re Looking For

A dynamic, transformational leader who will modernize and integrate corporate services, simplifying processes and raising performance as NHC grows.
Hands-on and ready to act, making an immediate impact by strengthening the finance function and building depth across the team.
An innovative, steady executive who brings fresh approaches to partnerships, funding, and procurement, and leads with confidence through change.
A coach and people builder who develops talent, especially Nunavut Inuit, and communicates complex issues clearly and respectfully.

Qualifications

CPA designation and at least 10 years of progressive senior finance and management experience, ideally in the public sector, a Crown corporation, or housing.
Strong command of public-sector budgeting, financial administration, and audit.
Knowledge of Nunavut, the Nunavut Agreement, and the roles of Inuit organizations.
Housing experience and fluency in more than one of Nunavut’s official languages are assets; an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Priority will be given to Nunavut Inuit who self-identify as being enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement, in accordance with the GN Priority Hiring Policy.

Salary: $160,374 to $229,106 per year, plus Northern Allowance and subsidized housing.

Closing date: November 25, 2026.

This position is a Position of Trust, a criminal record check required. AI will not be used in candidate screening.

To apply, submit your application to Phelps by clicking: https://phelpsgroup.ca/careers/31837/nunavut-housing-corporation-vp-finance-corp-services/apply/(opens in a new tab)

new_jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Head of Finance - R&D based in Canada.

We are looking for a strategic and hands-on finance leader to oversee the financial and banking infrastructure of a portfolio of fast-growing international technology businesses.

In this role, you will shape a multi-jurisdictional banking network, strengthen payment operations, and manage complex treasury activities across multiple entities.

You will drive liquidity management, optimize foreign exchange and transaction costs, and ensure reliable cross-border financial flows.

Working closely with founders and senior leaders, you will contribute to financial strategy, business performance, and investment decisions.

You will also build scalable treasury and finance processes from the ground up while developing a high-performing operational team.

This is an opportunity to take full ownership of a complex financial ecosystem and support the growth of ambitious digital businesses in a dynamic, international environment.

Accountabilities

Responsibilities

As Head of Finance - R&D, you will lead the development and management of the financial infrastructure, treasury operations, and banking partnerships supporting international technology businesses. Your main responsibilities will include:

Banking and Payment Infrastructure
Design and implement a flexible, multi-jurisdictional banking network for international digital businesses operating under demanding compliance requirements.
Identify, negotiate with, and onboard strategic financial partners, including leading banks, Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs), Payment Service Providers (PSPs), custodians, and financial platforms.
Negotiate favorable commercial terms, including transaction fees, payment terms, foreign exchange rates, and hedging instruments.
Establish backup banking relationships and alternative payment channels to ensure uninterrupted transaction processing.

Treasury and Liquidity Management
Manage multi-currency liquidity, working capital, cash pooling, and treasury operations across a group of legal entities.
Oversee complex international transfers through SWIFT, SEPA, ACH, and other payment networks, prioritizing speed, security, and cost efficiency.
Monitor and reduce treasury expenses, including FX spreads, acquiring fees, and banking charges.

Compliance, KYC, and Regulatory Strategy
Coordinate banking due diligence and maintain effective communication with bank compliance and risk teams.
Ensure the long-term stability of banking relationships and payment flows.
Support financial restructuring, corporate changes, and related banking and compliance requirements.

Financial Systems and Executive Partnership
Build integrated treasury and financial processes from the ground up.
Partner with founders and senior leadership on unit economics, ROI analysis, and financial modeling.
Recruit, lead, and develop the treasury and operational finance team.

Requirements

The ideal candidate combines senior finance leadership experience with strong expertise in international treasury operations, banking infrastructure, and financial compliance. You should bring:

At least 5 years of experience as a CFO, VP of Finance, or Head of Treasury in fast-growing businesses.
A proven track record of opening corporate bank accounts and establishing efficient payment processes.
Deep knowledge of international AML/KYC principles, cross-border compliance, and regulatory requirements across different jurisdictions.
Practical experience managing multi-currency funds, foreign exchange exposure, financial settlement instruments, and transaction cost optimization.
Strong negotiation skills and the ability to manage complex relationships with banks, legal advisors, and financial service providers.
Advanced English proficiency (C1/C2), with the ability to lead detailed, persuasive negotiations independently.
Strong strategic thinking, financial judgment, and the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-paced, international environment.
Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with founders and executive stakeholders.

Benefits

High level of autonomy: Full ownership of the financial and banking infrastructure, with minimal unnecessary bureaucracy.
Meaningful business impact: Direct involvement in launching and scaling new technology businesses serving millions of users.
Strong professional environment: Collaboration with experienced founders and talented engineering and marketing professionals.
Dedicated platform support: Access to more than 10 specialized teams providing expertise in recruitment, communications, finance, legal matters, and other operational areas.
Founder community: Opportunities to exchange practical knowledge and experience with entrepreneurs who have successfully launched multiple businesses.
Professional communities: Access to internal groups focused on product, marketing, engineering, and payments.
Learning and development: Training programs, professional courses, and opportunities to attend industry conferences.
Healthcare: Medical insurance.
